note: No AI code in this repo, so no ai_* labels. TMDB key is server-only and the Supabase key is the public publishable or anon key. .env.local.example holds placeholders only and no .env file is committed. Data access goes through Prisma in server actions that take the user from the Supabase session and scope every query by userId, so no IDOR was found. No mock data and no fake toasts in the main app. Every form posts to a real server action. The main risks are tables with no RLS and the open i18n editor server action that writes to disk.

labels.what: UserTitleEntry (each user's ratings, reviews and progress) is created in the Supabase public schema with no row level security in any migration. Prisma bypasses RLS, but the public anon key can reach the table through the Supabase Data API if public is exposed (the default)
UserProfile table (maps Supabase auth user ids to profiles) has no row level security
Title catalog table has no row level security, so anon key holders could insert or edit shared title rows that every user sees
CustomList table has no row level security
CustomListEntry table has no row level security

saveTranslations is an exported server action with no login or role check. Any visitor can call it and overwrite docs/i18n-table.csv on the server with arbitrary rows. The /i18n-editor page (page.tsx lines 4-5) is also open to everyone

CSV import writes any value starting with ( or function, and every key, into lib/i18n/en.ts and zh.ts unescaped. Text saved through the open i18n server action becomes source code the next time a developer runs import
Server rate limit is an in-memory Map per process: it only delays up to 2 s and never rejects, and it does not hold across serverless instances
Raw error messages from Prisma and TMDB are returned to the browser (same pattern in every action's catch block)
Public search page calls TMDB with the server key on every request, with no login or rate limit
Page says saving updates both language files, but the save action only writes the CSV. The TS dictionaries change only after someone runs the import script
TMDB search language is fixed to en-US while the app offers a Chinese interface
Rating range 1 to 10 is typed again in parseRating instead of using minRating and maxRating (lines 40-41)
Supabase publishable or anon key read from NEXT_PUBLIC env vars. It is public by design and no value is committed. It matters only because the tables have no RLS
